issues.description: Method name/signature inconsistency for the developer description: the problem statement and the template expect an instance method named swiftExperienceDescription(), but the solution defines a method named getExperienceDescription(). The solution's Client code still calls swiftExperienceDescription(), so the solution set is internally inconsistent (the Developer implementation and Client usage disagree). This mismatch will confuse students about which method to implement and makes the solution repository unbuildable as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name/signature consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the solution's getExperienceDescription() to swiftExperienceDescription(), or update the template/problem statement to require getExperienceDescription(). Also ensure the Client code calls the same method name (update Client to call getExperienceDescription() if you keep that name). This will restore consistency and make the solution buildable and aligned with the exercise description.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a Developer instance method named swiftExperienceDescription(), but the solution implementation defines and uses getExperienceDescription() instead. This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual operation (producing a printable Swift experience description) creates a mapping confusion: students will implement swiftExperienceDescription() as instructed, yet the solution uses a differently named method, and Client.swift in the solution still calls swiftExperienceDescription(), producing an inconsistent cross-artifact state.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name across all artifacts. Prefer keeping the name from the problem statement and template: rename the solution's getExperienceDescription() to swiftExperienceDescription(), update its uses accordingly (including the initializer), and ensure Client.swift calls swiftExperienceDescription(). Alternatively, change the problem/template to reference getExperienceDescription(), but keep names consistent across problem_statement.md, Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift, and Sources/DeveloperLib/Client.swift.
